This is an Appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, 'M.V.Act') by the Insurance Company against the judgment and award dated 14/01/2015 2 FA 269-2015.odt passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gondia (for short, 'the Tribunal') in MACP No.
109/2008 awarding the compensation of Rs. 4,34,000/- to the Respondent no. 1 against the Appellant - Insurance Company and Respondent no. 2, jointly and severally with 7% interest per Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd. Gondia vs Harikantabai Wd/O Laxman Chaure

1 annum.
2.
The deceased Jitendra Chaure was the son of Respondent no. 1.
He was a member of the Band Party in the District Gondia.

On 12/05/2008 at around 19:30 hours, when the deceased was proceeding with his colleagues at the place of event from the proper side of road, a four wheeler i.e.
Tata Sumo, which was owned and driven by the Respondent no. 2, gave dash to the deceased in a rash and negligent manner.
The deceased was hospitalized for treatment and he succumbed to the injuries.
A crime was registered for the said motor vehicular accident at the concerned Police Station.
The Respondent no
. 1 filed the Claim Petition under Section 166 of the M.V.Act against the Appellant and Respondent no. 2 for compensation.
The Respondent no
. 1 led the evidence.
By the impugned judgment and award, the learned Tribunal awarded the compensation.
3. Heard learned Advocate for the Appellant and 3 FA 269-2015.odt learned Advocate for Respondent no. 1. None for the Respondent no. 2.
Scrutinized the evidence on record.
4. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Appellant that, the driver of four wheeler was not holding a valid and effective licence at the time of accident.
The Appellant proved the said fact by examining the relevant witness.
There was a difference in the name in Form 'AA', which was brought on record, and Exh. 25 which was the copy of licence.
The learned Tribunal ought to have passed the order of pay and recover.
The Appeal be allowed.
5. It is submitted by the learned Advocate for the Respondent no. 1 that, the learned Tribunal has rightly passed the impugned judgment and award.
Further, he has no objection, if the order of pay and recover is passed.
6. In support of the Claim Petition, Respondent no. 1 led evidence.
The police papers in respect of the said motor vehicular accident are brought on record.
The said papers include the copy of driving licence in the name of Respondent no. 2 below Exh. 25.
The said copy is a part and parcel of the police 4 FA 269-2015.odt papers.

There is endorsement on Exh. 25 in respect of L.M.V./Tractor and date is shown as 27/06.
7.

The Insurance Company in support of their contention that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and effective licence, examined the witness from the office of Regional Transport, Gondia.
In the evidence of this witness, the copy of driving licence of the driver showing that, it was for two wheeler is brought on record at Exh. 35.
He was unable to say whether the driver was holding a licence to drive the four wheeler.
He volunteer that, had there been licence for four wheeler, there would have been entry in the record.
8. There is no challenge by the Appellant to the said Exh. 25.
The stamp at Exh. 25 is of the office of Regional Transport, Gondia.
In view of this Exh. 25 on record, no fault can be found with the observations made by the learned Tribunal that, the driver was having licence of L.M.V. which was dated 27/06.

As regards the contention in respect of variance in the name is concerned, except '@
Devendra', the middle name and the surname on both the licences is similar.
In view of above discussions, no interference is called for in the impugned 5 FA 269-2015.odt judgment and order
